artifacts.summary: Reproduces the Signal B --dispatched-agent exit-3 defect live against a real deploy-consumer repository and recommends resolving through .claude-extensions.json's per-extension source_dir field, preserving the existing agent-system/extensions/<ext>/agents/<name>.md resolved-path shape required by the recursion guard and dedup key.

memory_candidates.content: A deploy-consumer repository's .claude-extensions.json records, per loaded extension, an absolute source_dir path back to the source-store-holding repository's agent-system/extensions/<ext> directory on the same machine. Any script needing to resolve a source-store-relative identity string (e.g. agent-system/extensions/<ext>/agents/<name>.md for Signal B defect attribution) from a repository that does not itself hold the source store should read this field rather than globbing PROJECT_ROOT/agent-system/**, which only ever exists in the one repository physically hosting the store. Verified live against three real deploy-consumer repos (cslib, ModelChecker, .dotfiles) on this machine.

system-defect-record.sh's resolved_path (Signal B attribution) feeds three downstream consumers that all require its agent-system/extensions/<ext>/** shape to stay stable across repositories: the recursion guard (self_mod_match against orchestrator-critical-paths.json), the defect_key dedup identity, and the persisted attributed_source_path detail field. A fix to its resolution mechanism must reproduce that exact string shape rather than substituting a differently-shaped identifier (a bare agent name, or a deployed .claude/** path), or it silently forks the dedup/recursion-guard key space per repository for the same underlying agent file.
